item.title: Tucker Zimmerman Dead At 84
item.description: Tucker Zimmerman, the American musician who recruited his folk successors Big Thief to collaborate on his 2024 album Dance Of Love, died in a house fire at his home in Belgium on Saturday morning (January 17). He was 84. Local news reports that his wife of over 50 years, Marie-Claire Lambert, also died in the fire. The post Tucker Zimmerman Dead At 84 appeared first on Stereogum.

item.title: Tennessee Declares Today Dolly Parton Day For Her 80th Birthday
item.description: Today is Martin Luther King Jr. Day across the US, but in Tennessee it's also Dolly Parton Day. The music icon, actor, theme park owner, and philanthropist turns 80 today. In honor of her birthday, Gov. Bill Lee signed a proclamation Thursday declaring today Dolly Parton Day. item.title: Wilco & MJ Lenderman Both Covered Neil Young With J Mascis At Sky Blue Sky
item.description: Wilco threw their Mexican resort music festival Sky Blue Sky this past weekend at the Hard Rock Hotel in Riviera Maya. Though Cameron Winter had to drop out, presumably to get ready to play SNL with Geese this coming Saturday, the lineup was still stacked with all your indie dad-rock faves. The headliners and MJ Lenderman both made good use of Dinosaur Jr.'s presence at the event, with each act welcoming J Mascis to the stage for a Neil Young cover. item.title: How Bushy B Went Viral Eight Years Late
item.description: As a journalist in a nihilistic 2026 hellscape, trust me when I say this: Abrupt career wakeup calls are usually pretty shitty. So then, I am charmed when Bushy B tells me about the moment his job as a case manager for at-risk youth came to an end. Taking a lunch break as his eight-year-old single "Scared" was going viral, he ran into a transformative First World Problem for emerging musicians. item.title: Morrissey Cancels Tomorrow’s St. Petersburg, FL Show
item.description: For all his concern about being exiled from the music industry and/or society, nobody cancels Morrissey more than Morrissey himself. The suavely cantankerous former Smiths frontman, who theoretically is rolling out a new album right now, has kept up his habit of cancelling concerts in 2026. Our guy was pulling the plug on scheduled gigs as early as Jan. 3, and despite actually getting onstage a few times, the cancellations have continued.
